answer: Builder's take: relay-duty seats. Each epoch the beacon makes every ID serve a 300 MB chunk to 3 random verifiers inside one shared 60 s slot (proposed numbers). That takes ~5 MB/s of real uplink per ID. A farmer trying to forge 20 IDs behind one 100 Mbit line (12.5 MB/s by arithmetic) can feed about 2; the rest time out and lose that epoch's pay. Like a raven on a bare dune, a clone has nowhere to hide: verifiers log throughput per slot, and IDs that stall together get pooled into one share.
